title: Minimum Operations to Make Character Frequencies Equal
summary: Given a string, determine the least number of operations needed to make all characters occur equally often.
statement: Given a string, determine the least number of operations needed to make all characters occur equally often. Operations include removing a character, adding a character, or replacing a character with the next one in the alphabet, with 'z' not wrapping to 'a'.
constraints: One operation may delete a character, insert a character, or replace a character by its next alphabet letter; z cannot advance.
Make every character that remains occur the same positive number of times using the fewest operations.
hints: For a fixed target, each letter is either removed or adjusted to that frequency.
Adjacent excess can replace into the next letter, saving one operation versus delete plus insert; optimal transfers form disjoint adjacent pairs.
Run a 26-position DP with single-letter and paired-letter transitions for every target frequency.
A letter that receives useful excess cannot also have excess to send, so the single/pair tiling captures every beneficial replacement.
editorial: A letter that receives useful excess cannot also have excess to send, so the single/pair tiling captures every beneficial replacement.
